$comment: D4.39 — THE EIGHT REQUIREMENTS, CHALLENGED AGAINST MACHINERY THAT ALREADY EXISTS.
D4.38 derived what a satisfaction relation must express, from eight real cases. This asks the
question that must come before any schema: of those eight, which can the repository ALREADY
represent, which need a genuinely new primitive, and which are legal judgements no primitive
No schema is proposed. Nothing is migrated. The point of the exercise is to avoid inventing
machinery that has already been built and shipped somewhere else in this codebase.
status: AUDITED — no representation selected, no migration begun

legal_propositions.direction: SATISFACTION — a clause declares what it establishes
legal_propositions.vocabulary: proposition_id, statement, authority, applicability {always | position+value}, satisfaction {IN_THE_DOCUMENT | OUTSIDE_THE_DOCUMENT}
legal_propositions.$note: The youngest of the three and by far the weakest. 12 propositions, 3 implementing clauses.

evidence_propositions.direction: APPLICABILITY — evidence about the world gates a clause
evidence_propositions.vocabulary: subject_binding, admissible_provenance, continuing, evidence_valid_for_days, when_unknown; a seven-value EVIDENCE state vocabulary and a four-value APPLICABILITY one

concepts.direction: APPLICABILITY — a legal concept attaches clauses, rules and disclosures
concepts.vocabulary: requires_dimensions, attributes (typed enum/boolean/string), detection rules with {var, op, value} predicates, attaches, confirmation, unresolved_behaviour

the_headline.finding: Every requirement that needs a new primitive already has a WORKING PRECEDENT elsewhere in this repository — built, shipped and tested, pointing in the applicability direction.
the_headline.$what_that_means: The satisfaction layer does not need machinery invented for it. It needs machinery that exists to be turned around. That is a materially smaller and more reviewable change than designing a proposition system from first principles, and it is the difference between extending this architecture and replacing it.
the_headline.$what_it_does_not_mean: That turning it around is mechanical. An applicability predicate answers 'does this clause belong here'; a satisfaction predicate answers 'is this requirement met'. Same shape, different truth-maker, and the legal residue in the table below does not shrink at all.
the_headline.$corrected_in_D4_41: Overstated for B. 'Every requirement needing a new primitive has a working precedent' holds for the OPERATIONS; for B's dimension structure it holds only as a data shape nobody evaluates.

the_audit.how: clause.implements → proposition_id. Live on 3 clauses today.
the_audit.legal_residue: Whether the claim is true. Unverified against the clause text; see case D.

the_audit.how: Several clauses each declaring the same proposition, evaluated existentially. IP_OWNERSHIP_001 and IP_DEVELOPER_RETAINS_001 both satisfying 'ownership is specified' is exactly what existential satisfaction is for.
the_audit.$the_design_constraint_this_creates: Existential satisfaction must SURVIVE whatever is built for case B. A relation that becomes conjunctive by default breaks this case. The two must coexist and be selectable per proposition — and the choice between them is itself a legal judgement about what the proposition asserts.
the_audit.legal_residue: Whether the proposition is about specification or about outcome. F only works because 'ownership is specified' was framed that way.
What counts as discharge outside the document, and what evidence of it is admissible — which is the evidence layer's whole subject.

the_audit.how: implements already lives on the clause, which is the right location — specialising knowledge and declaring what it establishes become one authoring act.
the_audit.the_gap: Nothing requires the declaration. A new clause with no implements is indistinguishable from one that establishes nothing, which is the D4.35 failure exactly.
the_audit.precedent_for_the_fix: documentRequirements.admit already refuses knowledge records that do not declare their kind — the repository has an admission gate that makes silent omission impossible. The pattern exists; it is not applied here.
the_audit.legal_residue: None for the obligation itself. Enforcing a declaration is mechanical; its content is not.

the_audit.how: implements_review_status exists on every declaring clause, and the advocate review system built in this phase persists decisions with reviewer identity and enrolment.
the_audit.the_gap: Every claim reads draft-needs-legal-review, and nothing distinguishes a claim reviewed BY ITS AUTHOR from one reviewed by anyone else. Refutability needs a different reader, not merely a status field.
the_audit.precedent_for_the_fix: constraintScopeReviewService refuses a decision with no authority cited — the repository already has a review surface that will not accept an answer without its basis.
the_audit.legal_residue: The review itself. This is the case that cannot be automated at all.

the_audit.how_today: Nothing expresses 'these together'. Satisfaction is existential; gates and attaches are lists of what is affected, not conjunctions of what establishes.
the_audit.the_precedent: concepts.requires_dimensions is a conjunction across keys with disjunction inside each — {"role":["employer"],"event":["employ"]} means role AND event, any listed value within each. That is precisely the shape the IP grant needs: copyright AND patents AND trademarks, where each is satisfied by any of its own clauses.
the_audit.$so_the_primitive_is_not_new_in_shape: It is new in the satisfaction direction. The conjunction/disjunction structure has been authored, shipped and tested on the applicability side.
the_audit.legal_residue: Whether a trademark-only assignment establishes the proposition. The structure can represent either answer; only an advocate can choose.
the_audit.$corrected_in_D4_41: requires_dimensions is read by NO code. The precedent cited here is a declared data shape, not executed machinery, and this audit's test checked only that the shape existed. The operations B needs — one predicate, conjunction across a list, disjunction across alternatives — ARE executed inside resolveConcept; the composition is what is new.

the_audit.how_today: Satisfaction is a two-valued enum with no reference to document content. CORE_PURPOSE_001 discharges a scope requirement while deferring its substance to {{purpose}}.
the_audit.the_precedent: concepts.detection carries predicates of the form {var, op, value} with ops including eq and present, over field: and control: sources — and concepts.attributes types the values (enum, boolean, string, optional). Together they already express 'this holds when this field has this value'.
the_audit.$what_turning_it_around_means: Those predicates currently decide whether a clause BELONGS. The same predicate shape would decide whether a present clause SUFFICES. 'A payment clause stating an amount and a date' is expressible with machinery that exists.
the_audit.legal_residue: Which values count, and whether the proposition requires context at all. A rule asserting 'must specify payment terms' may or may not be discharged by a payment clause with no figure.

the_audit.verdict: NEW PRIMITIVE — PRECEDENT EXISTS, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ONE
the_audit.how_today: The satisfaction side is binary and has no room for 'about the proposition and does not establish it'. Silence and denial are the same fact.
the_audit.the_precedent: The evidence layer's seven-value vocabulary is the same distinction already solved: EVIDENCE_ABSENT says nothing either way, while MISMATCHED, INADMISSIBLE, AMBIGUOUS, STALE and CONFLICTING each say something different and none of them is a denial. Its own comment records that each was a distinct false positive and that collapsing any two recreates the bug.
the_audit.$why_this_is_the_strongest: It is not merely a shape to copy. It is the same lesson, already learned the hard way in this codebase, in a layer that was built because collapsing states caused real defects. The satisfaction layer repeats the mistake the evidence layer exists to correct.
the_audit.legal_residue: Whether a given clause is negative evidence. IPA_MORAL_RIGHTS_001 recording rights that survive assignment is a legal reading, not a structural property.
the_audit.$superseded_by_D4_40: Reclassified. G1 is solved by an existing pattern (authoring, not machinery); G2 is withdrawn as an instrument artifact. The 'strongest precedent' framing below described a requirement that does not hold as stated.

the_tally.$the_last_line_is_the_result: Nothing in the eight requires machinery this repository has never built. Three need an existing pattern turned around, two need an existing pattern applied, three already work.
the_tally.$corrected_in_D4_40: new_primitive_with_an_existing_precedent is B and E, not B, E and G. Case G moved out after D4.40 found the repository had already solved and recorded it.

what_no_primitive_will_settle.$this_list_does_not_shrink: It is the same length whatever is built. A schema that appears to shorten it has absorbed a legal judgement into a default.
judgements: Whether a clause's text discharges a proposition (every case).
Whether a set of clauses jointly suffices where none does alone (B).
Whether a proposition requires context, and which values count (E).
Whether a clause is negative evidence rather than weak evidence (G).
Whether a proposition is about specification or about outcome (F) — which decides whether satisfaction is disjunctive or conjunctive in the first place.
Whether an authored claim is true (D) — reviewable by a person, never by a mechanism.

what_this_record_does_not_do: It proposes no schema, no field names and no encoding. D4.38's scope holds.
It does not claim the precedents transfer cleanly. An applicability predicate and a satisfaction predicate share a shape and not a truth-maker.
It does not migrate anything or touch a satisfier list.

It does not decide whether to extend the legal-proposition layer, generalise the concept layer, or build a third thing. That is the next decision, and it now has an evidence base rather than a preference.

the_next_decision.question: Given that three requirements need an existing pattern turned around and none needs new machinery, is the right move to extend the legal-proposition layer with those patterns, or to generalise the concept layer to serve both directions?
the_next_decision.$what_makes_it_answerable_now: Before this audit the choice was between an imagined proposition system and the status quo. It is now a choice between two concrete bodies of working code, with a list of exactly which capabilities each would have to gain.
the_next_decision.owner: engine for the structure; advocate for the six judgements above, which are unchanged by whichever structure wins
